---
title: Displays and local dashboard
---

## Notebook and terminal

`progress=True` selects an anywidget notebook display when available, otherwise a Rich terminal display. Both show sampler phases, per-chain progress, variable-wise worst R-hat and ESS, and the controller's checks and verdict. Install `[notebook]` for notebook rendering. Notebook stop messages use the widget comm channel and a shared `RunControl`; frontend responsiveness depends on the host notebook's comm scheduling. For independent cancellation during a blocking cell, use the localhost dashboard or `start()`.

## Authenticated localhost

```python
handle = monitor.start(model=model, dashboard=True, progress=False)
print(handle.dashboard_url)
try:
    idata = handle.wait()
    # The dashboard remains readable until close().
finally:
    handle.close()
```

The server binds to `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port. A random per-run bearer token travels in the URL fragment, not the HTTP query. The browser removes it from history and sends it only in an `Authorization` header. Treat the full URL as a credential. Reloading without the fragment requires reopening the original URL.

State reads and stop requests require authentication. Stop is POST-only and validates Origin and Host; the service does not enable cross-origin requests. Static assets are bundled, with a restrictive Content Security Policy and no third-party scripts or analytics. All run-supplied names, errors and hints render as text, not executable HTML. Trace previews show at most 20 elements and 500 points per chain. They are diagnostic previews, not a replacement for posterior plots.

The server is local to the Python host. A notebook running remotely does not make that machine's loopback URL accessible on your laptop. Do not expose the server publicly or publish its token. Remote transport belongs in a separate application.

## Reusable presentation

`DashboardState` is a lock-protected, transport-independent event reducer with `show_phase`, `show_sampling`, `show_convergence`, `request_stop`, `finish`, and `snapshot`. Snapshots are independent JSON-safe copies. `dashboard_assets()` returns bundled HTML, CSS and JavaScript bytes. `static/renderer.js` exports `render(state, root)` for consumers of the same schema; it has no sampler or HTTP dependencies.

A consuming application owns authentication and transport. It can dispatch typed events to the reducer and serve these assets without importing any cloud dependency into pymc-monitor. The local HTTP service is only one adapter for that state.
